cap: Pelvic inflammatory disease is one infection moving upward along continuous mucosal surfaces: from the cervix into the endometrium, out through the tubes to the ovary and pelvic peritoneum, and sometimes up the right paracolic gutter to the liver capsule (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis). The damage that lasts is tubal scarring, which explains infertility, ectopic pregnancy and chronic pelvic pain.
teach: Follow the dashed red path: each number is the name the infection earns at that level. A patient can stop at any step, so cervicitis alone, endometritis with cervical motion tenderness, or a tubo-ovarian abscess are all points on the same line. Because the tubes are narrow and lined by delicate plicae, healing by fibrosis blocks or distorts them, which is why even one episode raises the risk of ectopic pregnancy.
